industry: Optometry practices and optical shops (comprehensive eye exams, glasses, contact lenses, pediatric vision visits)
words_and_claims_to_avoid: 'Board-certified by the [State] Optometry Board' when the board licenses but does not certify (e.g., Texas Optometry Board guidance) — name the real certifying organization if any
Disease-cure / 'reverses glaucoma/AMD' claims without basis; implied medical guarantees
'Free eye exam' that requires buying frames without disclosing the condition and usual exam fee (state rules vary; NJ explicitly restricts contingency)
Texas-style illegal 'free eyeglasses' inducements where banned (Texas Occ. Code §351.404 — verify state)
Holding Rx hostage or implying patients must buy glasses/contacts on-site to get their prescription (illegal under FTC Eyeglass Rule / Contact Lens Rule)
'Most insurance accepted' if false; typos like 'acceptes' from templates
Before/after vision miracles without typical-results care (16 CFR 255)
compliance_notes: FTC Contact Lens Rule (16 CFR 315): after a contact lens fitting, automatically provide the Rx copy whether or not requested; no extra fee, no required purchase, no waiver; confirmation-of-release recordkeeping rules apply for sellers with financial interest in lenses. FTC sent warning letters in 2025 citing penalties up to the then-current civil penalty amount per violation.
FTC Eyeglass Rule (16 CFR 456): provide spectacle Rx immediately after refractive exam before offering to sell ophthalmic goods; cannot condition the exam on purchase; no extra fee for Rx release.
Free/discounted exam ads: disclose usual fee, what the exam includes/excludes, and whether purchase is required — several state boards require this; some states restrict free eyewear premiums.
State optometry board advertising rules vary (price itemization for contacts/glasses, specialty advertising, certification wording) — client must confirm.
16 CFR 233/251: frame % off, second-pair, free fitting/trial conditions need bona fide prices and clear terms.
Privacy: mail creative should not imply use of confidential medical information; follow HIPAA for any patient storytelling (authorization).
39 USC 3001: no official medical bureau look-alike mailers.
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic: pride, relief, care, anticipation are fine when legal.
Only laws/compliance are hard limits (FTC Contact Lens Rule / Eyeglass Rule, state optometry boards, truthful pricing).
Every angle and emotion_by_offer combo carries sell_the_outcome_line.
Vendor ROI labeled agency-only unverified; never print as fact on a client card.
Prefer one clear offer + one real photo + one QR (roofing-round5 directional).
No age default; kids' offers OK when the offer is truly pediatric — not as a demographic stereotype.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: 'Free exam with frame purchase' common in gold vs state rules that restrict purchase-contingent free exams / free eyewear
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Compliance wins: follow FTC Rx-release rules always; follow the strictest applicable state board rule on free exams/eyewear; disclose usual fees.
Agency-only unverified; useful as existence proof of optical mail, not as printable lift.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: AOA annual-exam consensus messaging vs noted evidence gaps on interval
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: May inspire reminder angles; do not invent 'proven every adult must annually' causal claims on cards.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: 'Board-certified' market language vs boards that only license
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Compliance: name the true certifying organization or do not claim board certification by the licensing board.
